extracted.intended_audience: academic medicine leaders, biomedical researchers, institutional research administrators, and policy makers
extracted.subtask_description: Organizational mission and guidance for supporting biomedical research through policy, advocacy, resources, affinity groups, and professional learning that advance discovery-to-care translation while promoting ethical, equitable, and efficient research environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of supported research
rubrics_metrics.description: “supports the entire spectrum of biomedical research from basic discovery and translational science to clinical and population health research.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AAMC supports these areas through policy and advocacy initiatives, data and research projects, professional learning and networking opportunities, and the development of tools and resources. Emphasis is on enabling work 'from bench to bedside to community.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Research policies and regulations promote robust and ethical science
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAMC supports 'research policies and regulations that promote robust and ethical science.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy and regulatory engagement should aim to strengthen scientific rigor and ethical conduct. This is an explicit organizing principle for the AAMC’s science-policy work and underpins their advocacy and resource development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimize administrative burden
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAMC seeks 'to minimize administrative burden' in research-related policies and regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Efforts and recommendations should prioritize reducing unnecessary paperwork, duplicative processes, and other administrative obstacles that impede productive research while maintaining appropriate oversight and integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foster a diverse biomedical research workforce
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAMC supports 'a diverse biomedical research workforce.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initiatives, data collection, programs, and policy positions should advance recruitment, retention, and development of researchers from diverse backgrounds across career stages (e.g., graduate students, postdocs, MD-PhDs, faculty).

rubrics_metrics.name: Create an inclusive and equitable research environment across all career stages
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAMC advocates for 'an inclusive and equitable research environment across all career stages.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work, policies, and institutional practices should address barriers to inclusion and equity at trainee, early-career, mid-career, and senior levels. Examples include affinity groups, professional development, and targeted initiatives like 'Our Voices: Black Women in Scientific Research.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide professional learning and networking opportunities across career stages
rubrics_metrics.description: AAMC is 'committed to providing professional learning opportunities for biomedical researchers in every stage of their career.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offerings include webinars, meetings, conferences (e.g., Learn Serve Lead annual meeting), and other events designed to build skills, share best practices, and facilitate collaboration among researchers and institutional leaders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Convene and support affinity groups to connect stakeholders
rubrics_metrics.description: The AAMC convenes several affinity groups focused on connecting individuals who work in biomedical research or support researchers at their institution (e.g., GREAT, GRAND, CFAS, GCEC, FOCI, COF).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each group has a distinct role: GREAT (research training enterprise/forum for grad, postdoc, MD-PhD program leadership); GRAND (research leaders, link research advancement to health improvements); CFAS (represents faculty and societies); GCEC (foster environments where people of all backgrounds thrive); FOCI (forum for conflict-of-interest leadership); COF (promote compliance and ethical conduct with focus on research/lab issues). Affinity groups are mechanisms for discussion, policy input, and peer learning.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain portals for policy engagement and updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the 'Science Policy Hub' and 'Washington Highlights' to find current engagement opportunities and resources on issues impacting institutions and researchers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These resources are the AAMC’s channels for ongoing policy engagement, updates on legislation/regulation, and opportunities for institutions and individuals to engage with AAMC policy work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Priority science policy issue areas
rubrics_metrics.description: Key topic areas listed: Animal Use in Research; CMS Open Payments Rules and Database; Common Rule; Federal Clinical Trial Policies; NIH Data Management and Sharing; Reducing Regulatory Burden; Research Security and Foreign Interference; Single IRB for Multisite Trials; plus broader Science Policy Initiatives.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These subjects represent domains where AAMC develops guidance, advocacy, and resources. Work, comments, or institutional policies relating to biomedical research may be evaluated against AAMC positions or resources in these areas.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community-centered, multi-sector research and action (Center for Health Justice)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The Center sparks community-centered, multi-sector research, collaboration, and action to make the case for policies and practices that ensure all communities have an equal opportunity to thrive.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research and policy recommendations should prioritize community engagement, multi-sector collaboration, and justice-oriented outcomes. The Center of Health Justice is an AAMC initiative that models these priorities and offers relevant programs/resources.
